outcome: Singleton live births after vaginal delivery
Type of obstetric treatment performed (vaginal delivery, cesarean section, euthanasia)
cohort: The study participants were 119 Holstein-Friesian cows experiencing veterinary-assisted dystocia in the Azores islands, Portugal.
finding: Uterine torsion represented 24.4% of total assisted dystocia, and singleton live births after vaginal delivery were more probable in cows with uterine torsion compared to the remaining cows with other dystocia.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery after uterus reposition was more likely to occur in cows with uterine torsion, resulting in singleton live births compared to dams presenting other dystocia.
cross-section timing: Cases were accessed between September 2012 and February 2013
